name: encoding.json
doc:
json.Format / json.Parse use compile-time reflection: inside these generic
functions `reflect.Fields<T>()` loops are unrolled per field and the
`if reflect.TypeOf<T>().Kind == ...` tests are resolved at compile time,
so every instance is straight-line code for its type. Library code names
other namespaces by their full path (it is instantiated in user scope).

The text is parsed by the C runtime (runtime/src/std_json.c, ABI.md 17.4)
into one arena document of nodes; a Value is a node of such a document
and Parse<T> walks the nodes directly, allocating Zell strings only for
the string fields of the destination. Format<T> appends to a runtime
writer (rtW*). Error paths are built only when a value is wrong.

items.name: Decode
items.doc: Decodes a dynamic Value into a T.
items.summary: Decodes a dynamic Value into a T.

items.name: Format
items.doc:
Compact JSON text of v (structs by their fields and @json(name, skip,
omitEmpty), slices and arrays, maps (keys sorted), pointers, strings,
numbers, bools, plain enums by variant name, json.Value, any holding
those). Nil slices, maps and pointers are null; an empty slice is [].
items.summary: Compact JSON text of v (structs by their fields and @json(name, skip, omitEmpty), slices and arrays, maps (keys sorted), pointers, strings, numbers, bools, plain enums by variant name, json.Value, any holding those).

examples.name: ExampleFormat
examples.code:
println(json.Format(Item{Name: "pen", Price: 1.5, InStock: true}))
println(json.Format([1, 2, 3]), json.Format("a\"b"))

items.name: FormatIndent
items.signature: func FormatIndent<T>(v T, prefix string, indent string) string
items.doc:
FormatIndent is Format with Go's MarshalIndent layout: each element or
pair on a new line that starts with prefix and one indent per nesting
level; "key": value; empty containers stay {} and []. The first line
has no prefix.
items.summary: FormatIndent is Format with Go's MarshalIndent layout: each element or pair on a new line that starts with prefix and one indent per nesting level; "key": value; empty containers stay {} and [].

items.name: Parse
items.doc:
Parses a JSON text into a T (structs by their fields and @json, slices,
maps with string keys, pointers, strings, numbers, bools, plain enums by
variant name, json.Value, any). Errors name the path: "users[2].id: ...".
items.summary: Parses a JSON text into a T (structs by their fields and @json, slices, maps with string keys, pointers, strings, numbers, bools, plain enums by variant name, json.Value, any).

examples.name: ExampleParse
examples.output:
1 cup 3 false
Price: expected number, found string

items.name: ParseValue
items.doc:
Parses a JSON text into a dynamic Value. Syntax errors read "json: <what>
at offset N" (lexical) or "json: expected , or ] in an array, found
number 2", "json: unexpected end of input" (grammar); nesting deeper than
512 containers is "json: nesting too deep".
items.summary: Parses a JSON text into a dynamic Value.

examples.name: ExampleParseValue
